key_insight: CT–CS energy alignment governs the trade-off between charge generation and voltage loss in organic photovoltaics, while triplet recycling determines whether that balance survives at device level.
engineering_relevance: The model suggests targeting LE–CT offsets of 0.15–0.20 eV, weakly exothermic CT–CS offsets of 0.05–0.075 eV, and CT–T offsets no greater than about 0.1 eV.
method: Couple singlet and triplet exciton kinetics with device-scale drift–diffusion.
Solve state populations and reversible transitions self-consistently for transient and steady-state responses.
Evaluate energy-offset and triplet-transfer effects on generation, recombination, voltage loss, and extraction.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reproduction of triplet-mediated recombination in PM6:Y6 and material-dependent triplet recycling in D18:NFA blends, but provides no quantitative accuracy metrics.
watch_item: This is a physics-based model, not an AI method; its proposed design windows require material-specific validation.
paper_title: Device Model Linking Singlet and Triplet Spin-State Properties to Organic Photovoltaic Device Characteristics
